sections.heading: C — Intersections and interchange layouts
sections.markdown:
## C — Intersections and interchange layouts

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A60
A right-turning driver must yield when a bicycle already occupies the bicycle and turning-vehicle merging area. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A60
A bicyclist must move left when a car already occupies the bicycle and turning-vehicle merging area. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A60
Green pavement emphasizes places where different traffic movements cross one another. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A60
Some bicycle lanes and their extensions through intersections are painted green for added emphasis. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A60
At a green bicycle-lane crossing area, drivers must watch for bicycles. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A60
Bicyclists in a green bicycle-lane crossing area must be aware that vehicles cross the bicycle lane there. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A60
At a railroad crossing, drivers should listen and look in both directions for trains and their warning signals. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A60
Do not proceed through a railroad crossing until certain that doing so is safe. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A60
When a railroad stop is required, the handbook says the driver should stop at least fifteen feet and no more than fifty feet from the nearest rail. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A60
In the handbook's stated scenario, a freight train with one hundred fifty cars traveling fifty miles an hour has a stopping distance of seven thousand feet, given as one and one-third miles. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A61
Railroad approaches are often marked on the pavement with an X and the letters RR. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A61
Railroad crossbuck signs are found at most crossings. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A61
Flashing railroad warning lights are often combined with crossbuck signs at busy road crossings. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A61
Active flashing railroad warning lights require a stop, and further movement is allowed only when safe. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A61
Never drive through, beneath or around a railroad gate that is down or being lowered. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A61
Expect a train at any time and approach every railroad crossing carefully. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A61
Never stop while any part of the vehicle is on railroad tracks. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A61
In traffic, do not enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough room beyond it for the vehicle's full length. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A61
Do not ignore a railroad warning signal or drive around lowered gates even when no approaching train is visible. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A61
Do not change gears while crossing railroad tracks because doing so may stall the vehicle there. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A61
Never try to beat a train to a crossing. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A61
Before proceeding over multiple railroad tracks, make sure another train is not approaching on a different track. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A61
Watch for buses and trucks that are required to stop at railroad crossings, since some must stop at every crossing. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A61
Look in both directions when approaching railroad tracks even if the flashing warning signal is not working. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A62
A roundabout is a one-way circular junction entered and exited by turning right. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A62
The common roundabout warning sign shows an arrow in a circular pattern. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A62
Drivers entering a roundabout must yield to vehicles already circulating in it. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A62
Enter a roundabout counterclockwise and merge into its circulating traffic regardless of whether the desired route is right, left, straight or a U-turn. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A62
Slow down when approaching a roundabout and keep the speed low while using it. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A62
Obey the traffic signs and pavement markings at a roundabout. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A62
Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists both when entering and when leaving a roundabout. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A62
Yield to traffic approaching from the left that is already circulating in a roundabout. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A62
Use the right turn signal as the roundabout exit approaches. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0062]

Misconceptions: A roundabout requires yielding to circulating traffic, and an accidental SPUI exit cannot be corrected by driving straight across to reenter.
Mnemonic: Look, yield and follow is a teaching reminder for crossing hazards and the marked route.
Glossary: A roundabout is a one-way circular junction; a thru-turn replaces a direct left; SPUI means single point urban interchange; DDI means diverging diamond interchange.
Dynamic facts: active crossing conditions and local signal instructions are not frozen as invented schedules or timings.
